newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: HANSON HITTING ASIAN TOURIST NUMBERS IN QLD
The author of the latest Queensland Development Report says the number of Asian tourists visiting the state has fallen for the first time in 10 to 15 years.
Development consultant, Alan Midwood, says the downturn began last November.
Mr Midwood says it seems too much of a coincidence for it not to be attributed to comments made by Federal Independent M-P, Pauline Hanson.
He says the downturn began a month or two after Miss Hanson's maiden speech in Parliament, at a time when a lot of bad publicity about race relations in Australia was going out to Asia.
VIC ORCHARDS MAY HAVE TO START LAYING-OFF STAFF
Victoria's Natural Resources Department will treble its effort in surveying two million fruit trees in the Goulburn Valley for signs of the fireblight disease.
At a meeting of 300 fruitgrowers in the Goulburn Valley last night, the department defended the pace of the surveys to date.
Department officials believe the surveys will be completed by the end of next week.
But one fruit grower, Andrew Prentice, says cash flow problems are already taking their toll on orchardists.
Mr Prentice says growers will be forced to lay staff off by the end of this week.
UNEMPLOYED CAN BE FORCED ONTO WORK-FOR-THE-DOLE SCHEMES
The Federal Government says there'll be added incentives for unemployed people taking part in the work-for-the-dole scheme, due to get underway from October.
The Coalition's legislation has passed through the House of Representatives last night and will be debated in the Senate next month.
The legislation leaves the way open for all unemployed people to be forced to join the program, with penalties for dole recipients refusing to take part.
The office of the Minister responsible, David Kemp, says there'll also be incentives to join pilot projects.
Dr Kemp's office says unemployed people who have failed the dole activity test will have their benefits restored if they volunteer for a work-for-the-dole project.
The Government says it will also set up a small committee involving people well known in the community to select successful pilot projects.
HOWARD ON UK & US VISITS NEXT MONTH
The Prime Minister will visit his British and American counterparts a two week trip next month.
John Howard will meet with the Queen, new British Prime Minister Tony Blair, and Cabinet members in London for discussions on pursuing common interests between the two countries.
He'll then head to Washington where he'll meet with U-S President Bill Clinton and members of the U-S Congress.
Mr Howard says the visit will build on the success of President Clinton's recent visit to Australia in developing strong relations and co-operation.
The Prime Minister will end his trip in New York, where he'll meet the business and financial community to discuss Australia's economic reform agenda, and trade and investment links.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
